claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with a basic question:

**How many children are you asking about, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm asking about my child Alex, who is 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have a child named Alex who is 16 years old.

Since Alex is 16, the eligibility rules are a bit different. Let me ask:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (This could include things like school, college, university, or an approved apprenticeship or training course.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. They finished school but haven't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Since Alex is 16 and is not currently in approved education or training, there may still be an opportunity for you to claim Child Benefit, but only for a limited period.

Let me ask:

**Has Alex registered with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services since leaving education?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't registered with a careers service or the armed forces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 16 years old
- Alex is not in approved education or training
- Alex has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services

Unfortunately, this means you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. 

According to the Child Benefit rules, you can normally only continue to claim for a child aged 16 or over if they remain in approved education or training. Additionally, if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training, you can only apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if they register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

Since Alex has done neither of these things, Child Benefit eligibility for Alex would have ended when they left school.

**Before I provide my final assessment, I should ask: is there any possibility that Alex might register with a careers service or the armed services in the near future, or is there anything else about Alex's situation I should know about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there's nothing else. Alex hasn't made any plans to register with those services.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to provide you with my final assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Summary

**You are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 16 years old
- Child Benefit normally ends when a child turns 16, unless they remain in approved education or training
- Since Alex has left school and is not in any approved education or training, the standard eligibility has ended
- There is a 20-week extension available if a 16 or 17 year old registers with a careers service or the armed services, but Alex has not done so

If Alex's circumstances change in the future (for example, if they enrol in education, training, or register with a careers service), you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. If that happens, you're welcome to reach out for another assessment.
